history.summary: NOT A HINDU TEMPLE - a ghat, not a built temple (keep-or-drop decision needed): Iphi-Pani Ghat is a riverside spot on the Dibang river near Roing, described across travel sources as a scenic waterfront for fishing, angling, picnics and photography; one source calls it a 'revered pilgrimage site' with religious significance for the local community, another claims a local hot spring with medicinal properties - neither claim is corroborated elsewhere, so both are flagged (verify). No documented temple shrine exists at the ghat in any source consulted. Coordinates are those of Roing town and are approximate (verify the ghat's exact location locally).

name: Iphi-Pani Ghat
town_description: Roing is the headquarters of Lower Dibang Valley district in eastern Arunachal Pradesh, on the banks of the Dibang river. It is the gateway town for the Dibang Valley circuit, Bhismaknagar ruins, Mehao Lake and Mayudia.
tradition: Hindu folk pilgrimage ghat (riverside site, not a built temple)

travel.airport: Dibrugarh Airport (Assam), about 100-120 km; Tezu Airport (TEI) has limited scheduled flights.
travel.railway: Tinsukia Junction (Assam), about 90-100 km away, is the nearest major railhead.
travel.road: On the Dibang river near Roing town (exact location unverified - confirm locally).

visitor_information.best_time: October to April, the dry season; the river is most pleasant in winter.
visitor_information.opening_hours: Open natural site with no fixed hours; visit in daylight.
